name: Look & Touch (MAGIC touch / MAGIC tab)
summary: Gaze roughly places a cursor on a distant display, and the thumb on a handheld touchscreen fine-tunes it or steps through nearby targets before confirming with a touch.
howItWorks: Follows the principle 'gaze suggests, touch confirms'. Gaze positions a selection mask on the distant display; a touch on the handheld device freezes it. In MAGIC touch the thumb then moves the cursor absolutely or relatively within the mask; in MAGIC tab sliding the thumb cycles through the targets inside the mask, like a tab key. Further variants add a gaze-directed cursor with touch confirmation and local zoom lenses. In a study (N=24) with a Tobii eye tracker and a handheld touchscreen, all variants beat a plain gaze-directed cursor; MAGIC touch and MAGIC tab gave the best overall performance and usability, especially for small targets.
